problem: Find the equation of the left-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(5,1)$ and passes through the point $(-1,5).$

feedback.problem: Find the equation of the left-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(1,4)$ and passes through the point $(-1,8).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h,k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(1,4),$ we substitute $h=1$ and $k=4$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-4)^{2} & =4p(x-1).\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(-1,8),$ so we can substitute $x=-1$ and $y=8$ into the equation above and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-4)^{2} & =4p(x-1) \\ (8-4)^{2} & =4p(-1-1) \\ 16 & =-8p \\ p & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-4)^{2} & =4p(x-1) \\ (y-4)^{2} & =4(-2)(x-1) \\ (y-4)^{2} & =-8(x-1).\end{aligned}
$$
